It's meant to be ambiguous. However, I can tell you more-or-less what happened:

D-67895 is pretty smart, as well as being a sick sociopath. He had enough exposure to the Foundation to learn about more than one SCP, probably from researcher's comments. So when he typed DO EVERYTHING WRITTEN ON PAGE ONE, referring to the long document he had written back in his cell under the pretense of taking notes about the era, he was referring to a list of commands something along the lines of the following:

 1) LOCATE INSTANCE OF SCP-████ UNCONTAINED BY FOUNDATION. 2) PERFORM RITUAL [REDACTED] ON FUTURE LOCATION OF SITE-15 3) [REDACTED] 4) PROFIT!

A routine audit of Foundation archives uncovered SCP-████, an anomalous hardcover edition of Slaughterhouse Five recovered from a used bookstore in Los Angeles, CA, in 1947. The book bears inscription by Dr. ██████ and the additional phrase “Miss me yet?” written in human blood.

item.title: Re: SCP-687
item.content:encoded:
It is proper grammar. "Present" can mean "to come forward as a patient" when used as a medical term. "Present with" generally translates out to "exhibited the medical symptoms of"

http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/present — Intransitive verb, meaning 3

So the phrase in question is equivalent to "Examples include one subject who exhibited bleeding of the fingernails in a medical examination after dreaming of unsuccessful attempts…"

item.title: SCP-687

Frog, "noir" is a genre of detective stories, a descendant of "film noir", a filmic style often seen in the classic detective flicks of the '40s and '50s (sometimes starring Humphrey Bogart). Noir tales feature a hard-boiled detective, corrupt officials, large criminal organizations, and police interrogation techniques that might be regarded as a bit crude and violent by the KGB.

LA Noire (note the misspelling in the title) is called that because it's meant to evoke the spirit of noir stories.

Thus endeth today's lesson on the history of popular culture. I hope you were taking notes, because it might be on the final.
